feeds.what: every contest of the election in one document: statewide offices (14), federal offices (39: US Senator + 38 US Representatives), district offices (531: 16 State Senator, 150 State Representative, State Board of Education, courts), the statewide header (counties/polling places reporting, last updated), plus lookups and an office summary that also cover county-level offices
feeds.notes: A JSON envelope whose values are BASE64-encoded JSON: {"Version":"enr/53815/117/", "Districted":"<b64>", "Federal":"<b64>", "Home":"<b64>", "Lookups":"<b64>", "OfficeSummary":"<b64>", "Race":"<b64>", "StateWide":"<b64>", "StateWideQ":"<b64>", "ReportList":"<b64>", "ElementControl":"<b64>"}. Decode each value separately. 283,007 bytes gzipped. Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store. Home.RefreshTime = 5 (the site's refresh interval, presumably minutes). I saved the decoded sections beside it as election-53815.<Section>.decoded.json; those are derived by base64-decoding, byte for byte, not fetched.

feeds.what: list of elections with their ids (by year and type)
feeds.notes: {"upload":"<b64 JSON>"}. Decoded: electionInfo[year][typeCode][id] = {ID, N (name), O ('Y'/'N', looks like official), Y, ET, EC ('SW' statewide, 'PS' partial/special)}, plus currentelectionInfo.

election_id: 53815 = '2026 NOVEMBER GENERAL ELECTION' (electionInfo['2026']['GE']['53815']). It is the last path segment of the API URL. The feed's Version string 'enr/53815/117/' looks like an S3 prefix with a publish counter (117).
discovery: GET …/api/s3/enr/electionConstants, base64-decode .upload, and pick electionInfo[<year>]['GE'] (general), 'P' (primaries, one id per party), 'RU' (primary runoffs), 'S'/'SR' (specials). Do NOT rely on currentelectionInfo: when fetched it still pointed at 51031 '2025 NOVEMBER 4TH CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT', not the 2026 general.
cors: Broken for browsers: the API answers with TWO Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, 'https://openslate.us' (the request Origin reflected, with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true) and '*'. Browsers reject a response with multiple ACAO values, so treat it as needing the relay.
bot_blocking: API host goelect.txelections.civixapps.com (Cloudflare): relay User-Agent 200 on both endpoints, no challenge. The human page https://results.texas-election.com/races is different: relay User-Agent gets 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge page; a desktop Chrome User-Agent string with curl gets 200 (the Angular shell). The relay only needs the API host.
updated_field: Home.LastUpdatedTime = 'Nov 04, 2026 22:48:37' (inside the base64 'Home' section). No zone in the string; presumably US Central (Texas SOS, Austin) - not confirmed. Home.ElecDate = '11032026' (MMDDYYYY).
reporting_field: Statewide only, in Home: CountiesReporting {CR: 254, CT: 254}, PollingReporting {PLR: 5303, PLT: 5303} (polling locations reporting / total), PrecinctsReporting {PR: 202, PT: 200} (odd: reporting exceeds total, so do not trust it). Races in StateWide/Federal/Districted carry no per-contest reporting counts, only T (total votes) and per-candidate V (votes), EV (early votes), PE (percent).

titles.us_senate: U. S. SENATOR  (note the spaces after the periods and a trailing space in the feed: 'U. S. SENATOR ')
other_statewide: COMMISSIONER OF THE GENERAL LAND OFFICE
JUDGE, COURT OF CRIMINAL APPEALS, PLACE 3

choice_format: Races[].Candidates[]: {"ID": 39537, "N": "GREG ABBOTT (I)", "P": "REP", "V": 4524527, "PE": 45.67, "C": "#E30202", "O": 1, "EV": 3421415, "LN": "ABBOTT", "FN": "GREG"}. Names ALL CAPS; an incumbent has ' (I)' appended to N (LN/FN are clean). P is the party code: REP, DEM, LIB, and 'W' for a declared write-in candidate. V = total votes, EV = early votes (a subset of V), PE = percent (0-100, precision varies by section), O = ballot order. No measures on this ballot: StateWideQ decodes to {"OffType":null,"OffTypeID":null,"Races":[]} (Texas votes on constitutional propositions in odd-year November elections; Lookups.OfficeType has an id 2077 'STATEWIDE PROPOSITIONS' for them).
district_field: In the title N, and also as a number: Races[].SO (sub-office) is the district for districted offices ('U. S. REPRESENTATIVE DISTRICT 19' has SO 19, 'STATE REPRESENTATIVE DISTRICT 1' has O 51, SO 1), with O the office code (4 = US Representative, 3 = US Senator, 10 = Governor, 51 = State Representative, 80 = a court). Lookups.Office[] maps ID -> ON (name), OT (office type id), SO, SSO.
terms: none found (the API and the Angular shell carry no terms statement; I did not search sos.state.tx.us for a general policy page).
